Upstream: https://github.com/syoyo/tinyvdb
Commit:   e52e6bb969c71f8dc0325ea5972ddc32cd213b61 (branch main; includes
          portable flood-fill popcount, Windows inline fixes, and portable
          sparse-mesher bit scans)
Files:    the src/ subset needed by tvdb_mesh_to_level_set,
          tvdb_level_set_to_tet_mesh / tvdb_sdf_to_tet_mesh,
          tvdb_grid_volume_to_mesh, the volume access used by usdVol
          (tvdb_read_grid, tinyvdb_volume, tvdb_grid_to_nanovdb) and the I/O:
          tinyvdb_io.h (+ tinyvdb_io.c wrapper, lightusd's own), checked,
          mc_tri_table, mesh, mesh_conversion(.inl), ops.h, ray.h, sdf_tree,
          sparse, sparse_tools, sparse_tree, stats.h, tetmesh, tet_refine,
          tet_graded, thread,
          to_nanovdb (+ third_party/nanovdb/PNanoVDB.h, Apache-2.0, OpenVDB
          contributors), tree, tree_internal, volume, winding, tvdb_memory,
          lifecycle; and
          gpu_compute(.h, .c, _internal.h), nanovdb_device.h (+ generated string),
          built only with
          LIGHTUSD_TINYVDB_GPU.
Local:    CPU SDF allocation-aware entry points are local: tinyvdb_work.h plus
          mesh/BVH, mesh_conversion, winding, sparse_tools, sparse_tree and tree
          helpers pass an operation allocator through all generation scratch and
          retained output. Old entry points preserve default allocation. The new
          callbacks track their own block sizes (scratch frees/reallocs may pass
          zero for the previous size); the allocator must outlive owning outputs.
          Bounded sorts use deterministic in-place heapsort. grid_destroy_owned
          now uses the grid's allocator for its descriptor as well as its tree.
          Local tet-quality/balance changes are not yet upstreamed.
          tinyvdb_io.c is LightUSD's wrapper, not upstream's parser. tinyvdb_io.h
          adapts includes to ../miniz.h, ../../lz4/lz4.h and ../zstd.h.
          tinyvdb_sparse_tools.c also carries LightUSD commit dad7e2b7's CPU
          mesher optimization: detect shell isovalue crossings while gathering
          the shell, avoiding a redundant full-box scan. tinyvdb_tetmesh.c
          parallelizes stuffing over z slabs for pools with multiple workers;
          each slab uses compact local maps and the final merge follows the
          original z/y/x traversal, preserving byte-identical output. Its
          multi-worker warp now uses ordered corner/center wavefronts over
          increasing coordinate sums, preserving serial neighbor dependencies
          and byte-identical output across worker counts.
Update:   Vendored upstream source files now match main at e52e6bb, except
          for the LightUSD I/O adaptations and CPU changes described above.
          The upstream delta since 9217101 adds portable popcount/ctz helpers
          and compiler-specific NanoVDB force-inline handling. The selected
          source closure is unchanged, so cmake/lightusd-tinyvdb.cmake needs no
          source-list update. Recheck the dependency closure when syncing later
          revisions (link a probe calling the entry points above).
